topics.title: Sudden Weight Loss and Obsessive Fantasies
topics.summary: A man recounts a year-long disappearance marked by dramatic weight loss, accompanied by obsessive thoughts centered on his appearance and repeated fantasies involving women he perceives as attractive. He describes seeking specific attention from others while fixating on perceived physical shortcomings, highlighting anxieties about being viewed negatively.

topics.title: Stern and King Discuss Zookeeper Ratings
topics.summary: Howard Stern and Larry King discuss a zookeeper’s dismissive response to declining ratings, where the zookeeper criticized Stern for not having a TV show and refusing to offer free videotapes of his broadcasts.

topics.title: Philadelphia Zoo & Sober Sam Tennyson
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, hosts discuss an alarm at the Philadelphia zoo and potential power outages while attempting to secure free admission. They then shift into conversations about vacation plans, Howard’s frustration with scheduling delays, and Sam Tennyson's sobriety after 32 days.

topics.title: Tennyson’s Uncertain Sobriety
topics.summary: The broadcast features conflicting accounts of Sam Tennyson's attempts at sobriety, with Jim Jensen boasting about his success while others reveal he relies on sedatives. Howard discusses discrepancies in ratings data stemming from Virginia and Maryland collection methods, suggesting a reliance on incomplete information to assess public opinion.

topics.title: Sam’s Pool & AA Meetings
topics.summary: Sam maintains a heated pool despite high temperatures and struggles to lower the heat, discussing his sobriety through Alcoholics Anonymous meetings. He receives a large gift from Sally Marin while engaging in conversations with others about recovery and making inappropriate comments, leading to interactions with various individuals including a concerned listener and an attendee of AA.

topics.title: Radio Host’s Chaotic Conversation About Sam Kennison
topics.summary: A radio host engages in a nonsensical conversation with caller Dougie about musician Sam Kennison, repeatedly criticizing him and making bizarre claims including accusations of exploitation, fabricated stories involving computers and naked women in South Africa, and delusional fantasies about freeing the country.”} makes you smart now
